//: A block opens with `:name:` and closes with `:!name:`; a section opens and closes with `===`. Folding is by pattern rather than by indentation, because indentation is INSIGNIFICANT as of BMX 0.6 — a correct document may have none, and folding that depended on it would work on some correct files and not others.
//2: This keyed on `:::` until BMX 0.7 respelled the fence, so folding was silently dead in the shipped extension. A fold that does not appear looks like a feature that was never there, which is why nobody reports it. Found because BMX hit the same defect in their own config and said so.
//3: A one-liner — `:span: class=box :!span:` — must NOT start a fold, or it opens one that never closes and everything below it folds into it. The `[^:]*$` tail is what excludes a line that closes itself.
